title: Johnson–Lindenstrauss flattening lemma
statement:
Let $0 < \varepsilon < 1$, let $n \ge 2$ be an integer, and let $k$ be a target dimension satisfying $k \ge 32\,\log n / \varepsilon^2$. Then for every finite set $V$ of at most $n$ points in $\bbr^d$ there exists a linear map $f \colon \bbr^d \to \bbr^k$ such that every pair $u, v \in V$ has its squared distance preserved up to a factor $\varepsilon$:
\[
  (1 - \varepsilon)\,\|u - v\|^2 \;\le\; \|f(u) - f(v)\|^2 \;\le\; (1 + \varepsilon)\,\|u - v\|^2.
\]
hypotheses_covered: V is a finite set of points in ℝ^d
replaced:
Rademacher ($\pm 1/\sqrt{k}$ entries) analogue of \texttt{johnson\_lindenstrauss}:
same hypotheses on $\varepsilon$, $n$, $k$, and $V$, same conclusion---an
$\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$ exists---but now realized by a Rademacher
matrix.
